punchline: Two people with the same paycheck can be far apart in wealth, and Stanley's formula shows how far.
thirty_sec: Thomas Stanley's research on American millionaires found that visible spending and actual savings often don't match. To measure the gap, the book gives a yardstick: multiply your age by your yearly pre-tax income, divide by ten, and that's your expected net worth. Twice that or more makes you a prodigious accumulator of wealth. Less than half makes you an under accumulator. Many high earners fell into the second group, while many modest-looking households were in the first.
